content: Take this medication as soon as flu symptoms appear or as soon as possible after exposure to the flu. To prevent the flu, follow your doctor’s instructions and take oseltamivir, typically once daily for at least 10 days. The dosage is determined based on your medical condition and response to treatment. If you are unable to swallow capsules, consult your doctor or pharmacist about the liquid suspension form of oseltamivir. If the liquid form is unavailable and your doctor or pharmacist advises, you may open the capsule and mix its contents with a small amount of sweetened liquid, such as regular or sugar-free chocolate syrup, corn syrup, caramel topping, or light brown sugar dissolved in water. For optimal effectiveness, take this medication at evenly spaced intervals. To help you remember, take it at the same time(s) every day. Continue taking the medication for the full prescribed duration, even if your symptoms improve after a few days. Common side effects may include nausea and vomiting. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Rarely, the flu itself or oseltamivir may cause serious mental or mood changes, which are more likely in children. Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Before taking oseltamivir, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that can cause allergic reactions or other problems. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly needed. Oseltamivir passes into breast milk but is unlikely to harm a nursing infant. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk for serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Inform your doctor if you have received a nasal flu vaccine within two weeks before starting this medication, as oseltamivir may reduce the effectiveness of the nasal flu vaccine. In case of overdose, if someone has serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. This medication is not a substitute for the flu vaccine. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is within two hours of your next dose, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. For further guidance, consult your pharmacist or local waste disposal company. This information is a summary and does not contain all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for individual medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
